_readme: Task 8, Week 1. The fixed development dataset. Owner: Person C.
This file is the source of truth for development ids. Do not invent your own ids in a test;
use these. Thirty documents across seven collections: 2 publishers, 2 collections,
3 institutions, 14 catalogue items, 3 entitlements, 3 admin users, 3 feed settings.
Field names mirror Person B's @Document classes as delivered in ACADEMIC.docx (13 Aug 2026),
because DemoDataSeeder binds this file to them. If a name here does not match a field there,
Jackson binds null and the seed silently writes an incomplete document, so the integration test
reads documents back and asserts values, not just counts.
DETERMINISM. Every value in this file is a literal. No timestamps are generated at load time,
no ids are random and the BCrypt hashes are pre-computed, so two developers who run this get
byte-identical databases. That is the whole point of Task 8. Do not replace anything here with
NO FILES ARE ATTACHED. Every storageKey and indexKey is a 'seed/' prefixed placeholder and no
object exists behind it. Real content arrives with ingest in week 4. wrappedBek values are not
The four canonical books (item_42, item_env, item_ab6, item_stat) carry the ids, titles and
byte lengths frozen by the day 1 OPDS fixtures. team1 has already built against them.
Changing a byte length here breaks a published contract; DemoDataSeederTest asserts they still

_notes.cipherLength: 12 (nonce) + sizeBytes + 16 (GCM tag). Null here means the asset is not encrypted, so the number does not exist. B's Asset.cipherLength is a primitive long and cannot hold null, so DemoDataSeeder maps null to 0. The null is kept in this file because 'not applicable' and 'zero bytes of ciphertext' are different facts and the validator checks the first one.
_notes.indexTerms: Same treatment. Null means there is no search index at all; B's field is a primitive int, so the mapping writes 0.
_notes.storageKeys: storageKey, indexKey and wrappedBek sit on the ITEM, not on each asset. That is B's shape, and it differs from handbook section 06, which puts them inside assets[]. Consequence: a multi-format item cannot have a per-format storage key, so item_dual carries one key for two assets. Raised with B; see DAY4_TASK8_RUNBOOK.md section 3.
_notes.sizeBytes: The entity field name. The OPDS wire calls the same number originalLength.
_notes.isbn: item_42 uses 9780367211745, the ISBN frozen by the day 1 fixtures. Handbook section 06 illustrates the same book with 9780429288159, a different edition of it. The frozen fixture wins because team1 built against it.
_notes.entitlementVersion: No entitlement seeds a version. B declared 'private long version' with NO @Version annotation, so Spring Data optimistic locking is not active and the field is an ordinary number; the mapping writes 0. If B adds @Version later, 0 is still the only safe value: Spring reads a non-null version as 'this document already exists' and the first insert would fail with OptimisticLockingFailureException.
_notes.adminStatus: AdminUser.status is AdminStatus (ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, DISABLED), a separate enum from RecordStatus. All three seeded admins are ACTIVE, which is valid in both, but the mapping must use AdminStatus.
_notes.adminPassword: All three hashes are BCrypt strength 10 over the development password 'wokay-local-dev'. This is a documented development credential, not a secret. It is written down so nobody has to paste it into chat. The three hashes differ because BCrypt is salted; all three verify the same password.
_notes.institutionType: ACADEMIC, not UNIVERSITY. Handbook section 06 writes 'type': 'UNIVERSITY', but B's InstitutionType has seven values and UNIVERSITY is not among them: ACADEMIC, PUBLIC, SCHOOL, SPECIAL, GOVERNMENT, RESEARCH, CORPORATE. InstitutionType.valueOf('UNIVERSITY') would throw.
_notes.feedSettings: Seeded, one per institution, because B's FeedSettings landed and week 2's shelf feeds need it. Task 8's plan names five sets and does not include this one or 'collections'; both are declared additions. B's FeedSettingsPersistenceGuard rejects anything that is not exactly three shelves, so every row here has three, and an empty itemIds means a hidden shelf rather than an absent one.
_notes.auditLogs: Deliberately NOT seeded, although AuditLog and AuditLogRepository exist. An audit log records what actually happened; inventing entries would put fiction into the one collection whose value is that it is true. It also carries a 90-day TTL on 'at', so seeded rows would vanish and look like data loss. The admin console fills it as soon as anyone edits anything.

entitlements._seedWhy: COLLECTION scope, CONCURRENT. Covers item_42 and item_q7. The narrower scope, so it must beat the publisher grant below on item_42. Deciding this pair is OQ-5; this is the fixture-faithful option. To switch to the playbook option, move this row's institutionId to inst_ucl and change scope to PUBLISHER pub_crc.

PUBLISHER scope, UNLIMITED (copies null). Covers every Routledge book, so item_env and item_dual resolve UNLIMITED while item_42 stays CONCURRENT under the narrower grant above. That is scope precedence, testable straight from the seed. validTo is null, open ended, so the seed carries one of each.

ITEM scope, CONCURRENT. dev-sample-pdf's publisher (pub_crc) has no publisher/collection-level grant to inst_7f3 — item_ab6/item_stat/item_oa9 reach it via col_env2024 instead, which this fixture deliberately isn't in — so a dev fixture reclassified as ELITE needs its own narrow grant rather than inheriting one meant for real catalogue books.

feedSettings._seedWhy: The fully curated case. Three shelves, all populated, and every listed book is one Imperial can actually reach: item_42 through the collection grant, item_env and item_dual through the publisher grant, item_ab6 and item_oa9 because open access needs no grant. itemIds order is display order and the feed must preserve it exactly.

The zero-entitlement case. UCL bought nothing, so only open access can appear, and two of the three shelves are empty. An empty itemIds is a hidden shelf, which is the OPDS 'empty shelf is omitted, not emitted as an empty array' case with real data behind it.

Leeds is SUSPENDED, so no feed is ever served for it. The record exists anyway to keep feedSettings 1:1 with institutions and to exercise the unique index on institutionId. All three shelves are empty, which is the honest content for a customer whose account is paused.
